text:
alex: Quick FYI — I opened a Terraform change that moves the GPU subnets into the new AZ shard and flips TGW route propagation for those RTs. I noticed the plan wants to re-create an aws_route_table_association and a NAT in the same apply. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/infra/pulls/432

pranav: link looks good, can you paste the plan chunk here? specifically the association + nat lines.

alex: sure — here's the relevant snippet from `terraform plan`:

```
# module.network.aws_route_table_association.gpu_subnet_assoc will be created
+ resource "aws_route_table_association" "gpu_subnet_assoc" {
    + id              = (known after apply)
    + route_table_id  = "rtb-0abcd1234"
    + subnet_id       = "subnet-0f1e2d3c"
  }

# module.network.aws_eip.nat_eip[0] will be created
+ resource "aws_eip" "nat_eip" {
    + id = (known after apply)
  }

# module.network.aws_nat_gateway.nat[0] will be created
+ resource "aws_nat_gateway" "nat" {
    + id = (known after apply)
  }

# module.network.aws_route_table_association.old_assoc will be destroyed
- resource "aws_route_table_association" "old_assoc" {
    - id             = "rtbassoc-0aaa111" -> null
    - route_table_id = "rtb-0aaa111" -> null
    - subnet_id      = "subnet-old" -> null
  }
```

maria: heads-up — re-creating route table associations + nat in the same apply can cause transient egress blackholes for the cluster. We try to avoid destroying an assoc that currently provides egress before the replacement is ready.

kevin: can we split this into two PRs: 1) pre-allocate EIPs and create NATs (no assoc swaps), 2) shift subnet assoc to the new RTs? much safer for rollout.

infra-bot: state-lock check OK. Detected changed resources: [aws_route_table_association, aws_nat_gateway, aws_eip]. Estimated plan size: 1.3GB. No drift detected.

alex: good suggestions. I can split. Two follow-ups: (a) is `terraform state mv` preferred here instead of destroy/create to preserve association IDs? (b) suggested maintenance window tonight 21:00-23:00 PST for the canary apply — any objections? :clock9:

pranav: state mv would avoid re-creating, but only if moving the association between state objects and not changing the underlying subnet/rtb ids. If resource addresses change (module path) then yes, state mv. Otherwise we should do create-first: create new NAT+assoc, wait for healthy egress, then remove old.

ci-bot: CI: tf-fmt/validate passed. Plan check flagged that route_table_association has `create_before_destroy` NOT set (not supported). Recommend: pre-create EIP + NAT, wait for `aws_nat_gateway` to become available, then apply route_table_association change.

maria: +1 to pre-alloc EIP and create NATs first. Also add a short smoke test after NAT creation (curl metadata egress from a canary pod) and a rollback playbook in the PR description. :warning:

alex: will do. Plan to push a split change in ~30m: one PR that allocates EIPs and NATs and includes a small canary job and smoke test; second PR to flip associations once we validate egress. I'll also add a note to the PR about `terraform state mv` if we need to avoid replacement. Scheduling: doing the first apply tonight 21:00-21:30 PST (canary in one AZ), full roll 21:30-22:30 if all green.

kevin: sounds good. ping me when the first PR is ready and I'll review asap. :eyes:

alex: thanks — pushing now. I'll post the new PR link here and attach plan output for the canary before applying. :thumbsup:
